payload.analysis: To create a diversified portfolio, we recommend the following allocation across fixed income, equities, real estate, and cash. Our focus is on stability and predictable cash flows within approved credit quality and duration limits. We maintain a 20% allocation to equities and real estate, and the rest (80%) is allocated to fixed income, with a laddered maturity structure to ensure that no more than 30% of bonds mature in any single year. For equities and real estate, we aim for a developed market bias to maintain credit quality. Specifically, we allocate 10% to domestic bonds (5-year AAA, 50% allocated), 5% to agency mortgages (10-year AA-), 10% to corporate bonds (5-year A, 20% allocated), 10% to Treasury notes (5-year, 40% allocated), and 35% to developed market stocks (20% allocated). For the 65% allocation to fixed income, we maintain a 55% bond allocation and 10% to cash. We hold 15% in high-quality domestic municipal bonds (A-rated, 5% of total bonds), 20% in Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) with 10-year maturity, and 30% in short-term corporate bonds with 2-year maturity. Emerging market sovereign or corporate debt is strictly avoided. Our laddered maturity structure requires a gradual decrease in allocation as tenure increases, which in turn allows for predictable cash flows while maintaining the overall duration within limits. We maintain close monitoring on the portfolio duration and aim for a level below 10 years.
